cells.value: Dixie Fire origin: if it started today
Hypothetical: same origin and fire behavior as July 13, 2021, with resources and sensors as of Nov 7, 2026.
39.871306, -121.389439 (CAL FIRE official origin). Feather River Canyon above Cresta Dam, Butte County. Edit in Inputs tab to move the scenario.
CAL FIRE Dixie Fire incident page, https://www.fire.ca.gov/incidents/2021/7/13/dixie-fire

Assume the 2021 behavior: slow ground fire under a fallen tree from ~6:48 AM; ~600 to 800 sq ft by 4:30 PM; ~40 x 40 ft by 5:12 PM; ~2 acres by 5:42 PM; ~500 acres by 8 AM next day. No measured heat output on record.
CAL FIRE Station 36 Jarbo Gap, 17 km SW on Highway 70 (coordinates known). Also nearby by address: Concow 37, Concow Lake 38, Brush Creek 60, Berry Creek 61. See Stations tab.
TopoQuest, CAL FIRE Station 36 Jarbo Gap, https://www.topoquest.com/place-detail.php?id=2622345; NERIS, Butte County Fire Department stations, https://neris.fsri.org/departments/FD06007050/stations

Chico Regional Airport (~41 km W) is a CAL FIRE air attack and airtanker base; Aero-Flite also keeps a hangar there. Ag aviation operators in the Sacramento Valley (Chico, Biggs, Gridley, Colusa, Yuba City) can help only if carded and contracted as single engine air tankers; a Fire Boss version can scoop from large lakes. See Aircraft tab.

Butte County, Chico Air Attack Base, https://www.buttecounty.ca.gov/563/Chico-Air-Attack-Base; Aerial Fire Magazine, Aero-Flite hangar in Chico (2024), https://aerialfiremag.com/2024/03/11/aero-flite-establishes-hangar-base-in-chico-california
Feather River directly below; Cresta Reservoir 1.5 km; Poe Reservoir 7.8 km; Rock Creek Reservoir 15.7 km; Belden Forebay 30 km; Lake Almanor 42 km. See Water tab.

North Fork Feather River (Wikipedia mirror), https://ipfs.aleph.im/ipfs/QmXoypizjW3WknFiJnKLwHCnL72vedxjQkDDP1mXWo6uco/wiki/Feather_River_Canyon.html; Poe Dam, Wikipedia, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poe_Dam

Bald Mtn. (Butte) 1 is 12 km away and was pointed at the origin when the list was read. Bald Mtn. La Porte 1 (40 km) also covers it. Bald Eagle Mtn. 1 (15 km) is 10 deg off with a narrow view. See Cameras tab. Terrain line of sight not checked.
Confirmed positions; view can change (cameras pan)

Likely yes, through the camera, but only with a camera-first mode (not built yet): today's pipeline only checks cameras near a satellite hotspot, so it would alert at the first GOES-18 detection (estimated evening), with the camera adding evidence. With camera-first mode, a WATCH could fire once smoke rises above the trees, plausibly hours before the 5:12 PM call. A power-outage source (PG&E public outage map) could flag the 6:48 AM fault. See Timeline tab.
